original_question: How should one formulate a generalized Pythagorean theorem in a setting where one does not assume a pair of mutually dual affine connections?
target_in_paper: Section 5 (Hiroshi Matsuzoe), item 1: "How can we state the generalized Pythagorean theorem if we do not assume a pair of mutually dual affine connections?" This is posed immediately after the definition of bi-orthogonal coordinates on a Riemannian manifold. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly isolates the paper's exact open problem: formulating the generalized Pythagorean theorem after removing the assumption of a mutually dual pair of affine connections. That is the second question in Section 5, item 1. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
missing_details: The ambient setting is a smooth real Riemannian manifold (M,g), not an unspecified abstract framework. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
The problem is framed locally using two coordinate systems U=(U;x^1,...,x^n) and V=(V;y^1,...,y^n) on M. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
These charts are assumed to be bi-orthogonal, meaning g(∂/∂x^i, ∂/∂y^j)=δ_ij for all i,j=1,...,n on U∩V. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

The motivating comparison is the dually flat case (M,g,∇,∇*) in which such bi-orthogonal charts can be chosen as dual affine coordinates; your draft does not mention this comparison point. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

The intended scope is local and metric-based: the paper asks for a statement of the theorem using only the Riemannian metric and coordinate data, without presupposing affine connections. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

No extra algebraic parameters appear here: there are no ring/field choices beyond the usual smooth real-manifold setting, and no homogeneity, degree bounds, nilpotency assumptions, or asymptotic quantifiers such as "for all sufficiently large m". Those notions are not part of this problem. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
refined_question: Let (M,g) be a smooth real Riemannian n-manifold, and let U=(U;x^1,...,x^n) and V=(V;y^1,...,y^n) be local coordinate systems such that g(∂/∂x^i, ∂/∂y^j)=δ_ij for all i,j=1,...,n on U∩V (so U and V are bi-orthogonal). In dually flat information geometry, such charts can be chosen as dual affine coordinates. Without assuming any pair of mutually dual affine connections, can one formulate a local analogue of the standard generalized Pythagorean theorem using only the Riemannian metric g and this bi-orthogonal coordinate structure? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
justification: This is the nearest official formulation in the paper. In Section 5, item 1, Matsuzoe first defines bi-orthogonal coordinates by equation (1), then recalls that in a dually flat space they arise as dual affine coordinates, and then asks exactly how to state the generalized Pythagorean theorem without assuming mutually dual affine connections. The refined question makes those hidden hypotheses explicit while avoiding drift into the neighboring problems in the same section about existence of bi-coordinates, dual connections, or the definition of divergence. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
